problem:
Title: Schur's Lemma (Representation Theory)/Corollary

Let $\struct {G, \cdot}$ be a [[Definition:Finite Group|finite group]].

Let $\struct {V, \phi}$ be a [[Definition:G-Module|$G$-module]].

Let the underlying [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $k$ of $V$ be [[Definition:Algebraically Closed Field|algebraically closed]].

Let:
:$\map {\mathrm {End}_G} V := \leftset {f: V \to V: f}$ is a [[Definition:G-module Homomorphism|homomorphism of $G$-modules]]$\rightset {}$

Then:
:$\map {\mathrm {End}_G} V$
is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]], with the same structure as $k$.
proof_numbered:
0001 | Denote the [[Definition:Identity Mapping|identity mapping]] on $V$ as $I_V: V \to V$.
0002 | 
0003 | If $f = 0$, since $0\in k$ it can be written $f = 0 I_V$.
0004 | 
0005 | Let $f$ be an automorphism.
0006 | 
0007 | We have that $k$ is algebraically closed.
0008 | 
0009 | Therefore the [[Definition:Characteristic Polynomial|characteristic polynomial]] of $f$ is complete reducible in $k \sqbrk x$.
0010 | 
0011 | Hence $f$ has all [[Definition:Eigenvalue|eigenvalue]] in $k$.
0012 | 
0013 | Let $\lambda \in k$ be an eigenvalue of $f$.
0014 | 
0015 | Consider the endomorphism:
0016 | :$f - \lambda I_V: V \to V$
0017 | 
0018 | Because $\lambda$ is an [[Definition:Eigenvalue|eigenvalue]]:
0019 | :$\map \ker {f - \lambda I_V} \ne \set 0$
0020 | 
0021 | From [[Schur's Lemma (Representation Theory)|Schur's Lemma]]:
0022 | :$f = \lambda I_V$
0023 | 
0024 | :$\paren {\lambda I_V} \circ \paren {\mu I_V} = \paren {\lambda \mu} I_V$
0025 | 
0026 | :$\lambda I_V + \paren {-\mu I_V} = \paren {\lambda - \mu} I_V$
0027 | 
0028 | From [[Subring Test]]:
0029 | :$\map {\mathrm {End}_G} V$ is a subring of the [[Definition:Ring of Endomorphisms|ring endomorphisms]] of $V$ as an [[Definition:Abelian Group|abelian group]].
0030 | 
0031 | Let $\phi: \map {\mathrm {End}_G} V \to k$ be defined as:
0032 | :$\map \phi {\lambda I_V} = \lambda$
0033 | 
0034 | Then:
0035 | :$\map \phi {\lambda I_V + \mu I_V} = \lambda + \mu = \map \phi {\lambda I_V} + \map \phi {\mu I_V}$
0036 | :$\map \phi {\paren {\lambda I_V} \circ \paren {\mu I_V} } = \lambda \mu = \map \phi {\lambda I_V} \map \phi {\mu I_V}$
0037 | 
0038 | Hence $\phi$ is a [[Definition:Ring Isomorphism|ring isomorphism]].
0039 | 
0040 | But since $k$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] it is a [[Definition:Field Isomorphism|field isomorphism]].
0041 | {{qed}}
